title: Urgent delivery under a sustained WAN outage
why_local_cloud: T2 cannot use the deployed AWS endpoint (unlike T1/T8). The experiment IS a precisely-timed WAN cut: the outage is created by SIGSTOP-ing the cloud PROCESS the instant the lease is ingested and SIGCONT-ing it at mission end. A managed service (API Gateway + Fargate) cannot be paused, and its cloud<->edge link cannot be severed at a chosen instant. T2 also needs a short lease (compressed-timing pack) so C2's offline stall reaches a terminal state in seconds, and must drive the real supervisor in-process against a cloud whose process it controls. So T2 owns a LOCAL cloud; T1/T8 (no outage, no compression) use the deployed C1/C2 endpoints.
note: Edge = the real supervisor (C1 SLM / C2 relay / C3 rules) driven in-process. Outage = the cloud<->edge link cut by pausing the local cloud right after the lease is granted, held to end of mission. A persistent corridor obstacle forces a tactical decision. Compressed-timing pack (1 min urgent deadline + 8 s grace) so C2's lease expires within a short demo window; the mechanism is identical at production scale. RTT/loss/throughput/recovery are measured from HTTP probes and the traffic generator, never inferred from requested settings. Real tc/netem is applied only where tc exists.
